intro.title: Engineering work shaped
intro.lede: I am Peter Mwaura, an engineering student interested in systems, infrastructure, design, and the practical side of how things are made to work. I like projects that sit between technical depth, clear communication, and useful outcomes.

overviewItems.label: Positioning
overviewItems.value: Engineering student with strong systems instincts

overviewItems.label: Best Fit
overviewItems.value: Systems, product, operations, and multidisciplinary engineering roles

overviewItems.label: Approach
overviewItems.value: Frame the problem, prototype deliberately, refine with evidence

intro.recruiterHeading: I care about engineering that holds up outside the lab.
intro.recruiterBody: This site is structured to show how I think across systems, people, and implementation. The goal is not just to show what I built, but how I approach engineering problems with structure, usability, and context in mind.

about.title: Curious about systems, disciplined about execution.
about.lede: I am most energized by engineering problems that are technical, open-ended, and close to lived reality. I like taking something vague, breaking it into workable parts, and building toward a solution that people can actually use.
about.workingStyleTitle: I like turning complexity into something understandable and buildable.
workingStyleParagraphs: My best work usually happens in multidisciplinary settings where technical design, communication, and constraints all matter at once. I enjoy being the person who can keep the engineering grounded while still moving the project forward.
I care about engineering judgment. That means thinking about reliability, usability, tradeoffs, and whether a solution makes sense in the environment where it will actually live.
recruiterNotes: Comfortable with systems thinking and implementation detail
Strong presentation, documentation, and design communication habits
Ownership mindset in student-led and collaborative work
Able to connect engineering decisions to human and operational impact

education.title: B.S. Candidate in Engineering
education.description: Coursework spanning engineering analysis, systems design, prototyping, and human-centered problem solving.

education.title: Applied Project Experience
education.description: Worked on projects where technical development, iteration, and communication all mattered to the result.

education.title: Prototype and Team Leadership
education.description: Helped move ideas from concept to testable systems through reviews, coordination, and practical iteration.

about.quote: Good engineering solves the problem in front of you and still makes sense a year later.
about.quoteBody: That is the standard I try to build toward, whether the work involves digital systems, physical context, or the handoff between the two.

interests.title: I am drawn to engineering with context.
interests.lede: The work I keep coming back to usually sits at the intersection of systems, infrastructure, operations, and human use. I am especially interested in how engineering decisions play out in real environments.

cards.title: How parts interact under real constraints.
cards.description: I like thinking about whole systems: inputs, failure points, interfaces, and how design choices behave once conditions stop being ideal.

cards.title: Built solutions that stay useful over time.
cards.description: I am interested in the durability and maintainability of engineered systems, especially where function, environment, and access all shape the design.

cards.title: Turning concepts into something testable.
cards.description: I enjoy early-stage build work because it reveals whether an idea actually works, what assumptions break first, and what needs to change next.

favorites: Building first-pass prototypes with clear learning goals
Studying how systems behave under operational pressure
Translating engineering complexity into understandable decisions
outsideParagraphs: Outside of coursework, I pay attention to how engineering shows up in transportation, water, infrastructure, operations, and product systems that serve people at scale.
That is why this portfolio now leans into a cleaner, more modern engineering language: I want it to reflect broad technical curiosity, not just software identity.

projects.title: Work across systems, operations, and implementation.
projects.lede: These projects show how I approach engineering work that blends structure, experimentation, coordination, and communication. The emphasis is on ownership, decision-making, and what the build was trying to accomplish.

items.title: Engineering Portfolio Studio
items.description: Designed and built a content-managed portfolio system to present engineering work with more clarity, structure, and media support than a static student site.
bullets: Structured the site around project communication, recruiter usability, and visual storytelling
Built editable content flows, media handling, and multi-page rendering from a shared data model
Treated the site itself as a design-and-systems project rather than a simple web page
items.role: Systems design, content architecture, interface implementation

items.title: Event and Operations Planning System
items.description: Designed a structured system for managing schedules, registrations, and internal workflows for a student organization with growing coordination needs.
bullets: Mapped the operational flow across members, events, communication, and reporting
Built the internal logic and admin pathways needed for smoother coordination
Focused on reducing friction for organizers while keeping the system legible
items.role: Operations design, workflow modeling, internal tooling

items.title: Operations Insight Dashboard
items.description: Created a dashboard-style decision support tool to turn raw operational information into something easier to interpret, discuss, and act on.
bullets: Structured incoming information so patterns and bottlenecks were easier to spot
Designed outputs to support faster conversations and more confident decisions
Balanced visual clarity with the level of detail needed to stay technically honest

contact.title: Open to engineering teams building with purpose.
contact.lede: I am looking for internship opportunities where systems thinking, technical rigor, and practical problem solving all matter, especially in multidisciplinary environments.
contact.reachOutTitle: Let’s talk about the problems your team is solving.
contact.reachOutBody: If you are hiring for work that values strong fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to connect engineering to real use, I would be glad to connect.
